            selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
        else:
            selected_positions = selected_positions[:n_decap]
        
        offspring[i] = selected_positions
    
    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions
    # Research showed 10% perturbation rate works best
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.15:  # Increase to 15% to see if more exploration helps
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                neighbors.append(new_pos)
                
                # If we have valid neighbors, select based on geometric heuristics
                # Bias toward center (approximation of probe-bias when probe location unavailable)
                if neighbors:
                    # Instead of just center bias, try a more sophisticated approach
                    # that considers both center proximity and edge avoidance
                    center_row, center_col = grid_size // 2, grid_size // 2
                    
                    # Calculate scores for each neighbor based on multiple factors
                    neighbor_scores = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        
                        # Distance to center (prefer closer to center)
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)
                        
                        # Edge penalty (prefer not too close to edges)
                        edge_penalty = min(nr, nc, grid_size-1-nr, grid_size-1-nc)
                        
                        # Calculate score: closer to center is better, but avoid edges
                        # Higher score is better
                        score = (grid_size - dist_to_center) + edge_penalty
                        neighbor_scores.append(score)
                    
                    # Normalize scores to probabilities
                    max_score = max(neighbor_scores)
                    min_score = min(neighbor_scores)
                    
                    if max_score != min_score:
                        # Convert scores to probabilities using softmax-like approach
                        normalized_scores = [s - min_score for s in neighbor_scores]
                        total_score = sum(normalized_scores) + 1e-10  # Avoid division by zero
                        probs = [s / total_score for s in normalized_scores]
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                    else:
                        # All neighbors are equally good
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
                else:
                    # No valid neighbors, try a broader search in the grid
                    current_row, current_col = offspring[i][j] // grid_size, offspring[i][j] % grid_size
                    # Search in a larger radius
                    candidates = []
                    for dr in range(-2, 3):
                        for dc in range(-2, 3):
                            if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                                continue
                            new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                            if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                                new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                                if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                    candidates.append(new_pos)
                    
                    if candidates:
                        # Choose based on center proximity
                        center_row, center_col = grid_size // 2, grid_size // 2
                        candidate_scores = []
                        for candidate in candidates:
                            cr, cc = candidate // grid_size, candidate % grid_size
                            dist_to_center = abs(cr - center_row) + abs(cc - center_col)
                            score = grid_size - dist_to_center  # Closer to center is better
                            candidate_scores.append(score)
                        
                        # Normalize scores to probabilities
                        max_score = max(candidate_scores)
                        min_score = min(candidate_scores)
                        
                        if max_score != min_score:
                            normalized_scores = [s - min_score for s in candidate_scores]
                            total_score = sum(normalized_scores) + 1e-10
                            probs = [s / total_score for s in normalized_scores]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(candidates, p=probs)
                        else:
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(candidates)
    
    return offspring

    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Randomly select two parents
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Convert positions to 2D coordinates
        coords1 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent1])
        coords2 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent2])
        
        # Compute reference points for clustering using multiple strategies
        # Option 1: Centroid
        centroid1 = coords1.mean(axis=0)
        centroid2 = coords2.mean(axis=0)
        
        # Option 2: Random coordinate from parent
        random_idx1 = np.random.randint(len(coords1))
        random_ref1 = coords1[random_idx1]
        
        random_idx2 = np.random.randint(len(coords2))
        random_ref2 = coords2[random_idx2]
        
        # Option 3: Corner-based reference
        corner_ref1 = coords1[np.argmin(np.sum(coords1, axis=1))]  # closest to (0,0)
        corner_ref2 = coords2[np.argmin(np.sum(coords2, axis=1))]
        
        # Randomly choose which reference point strategy to use with fixed probabilities
        ref_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if ref_choice < 0.33:  # Use centroids
            ref1, ref2 = centroid1, centroid2
        elif ref_choice < 0.66:  # Use random refs
            ref1, ref2 = random_ref1, random_ref2
        else:  # Use corner refs
            ref1, ref2 = corner_ref1, corner_ref2
        
        # Calculate distances from chosen reference points
        dists1 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords1 - ref1)**2, axis=1))
        dists2 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords2 - ref2)**2, axis=1))
        
        # Divide each parent into two clusters based on distance to reference
        median_dist1 = np.median(dists1)
        median_dist2 = np.median(dists2)
        
        # Create masks for near and far clusters
        near_cluster1 = dists1 <= median_dist1
        far_cluster1 = dists1 > median_dist1
        near_cluster2 = dists2 <= median_dist2
        far_cluster2 = dists2 > median_dist2
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on fixed probabilities
        strategy_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if strategy_choice < 0.5:  # Traditional approach: near from one, far from other
            if np.random.rand() > 0.5:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent1[near_cluster1],
                    parent2[far_cluster2]
                ])
            else:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent2[near_cluster2],
                    parent1[far_cluster1]
                ])
        elif strategy_choice < 0.75:  # Take top half closest from each parent
            top_half1 = np.argsort(dists1)[:max(1, len(dists1)//2)]
            top_half2 = np.argsort(dists2)[:max(1, len(dists2)//2)]
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                parent1[top_half1],
                parent2[top_half2]
            ])
        else:  # Alternating positions based on sorted distances
            all_dists = np.concatenate([dists1, dists2])
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            sorted_indices = np.argsort(all_dists)
            # Take every other position from sorted list to get mixed distances
            selected_positions = all_positions[sorted_indices[::2]][:n_decap]
            if len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
                additional = all_positions[sorted_indices[1::2]][:n_decap - len(selected_positions)]
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional])
        
        # Handle case where we have too many or too few positions
        if len(selected_positions) > n_decap:
            # Randomly select n_decap positions from the combined set
            selected_positions = np.random.choice(selected_positions, n_decap, replace=False)
        elif len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
            # Fill remaining positions by random selection from either parent
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_positions, n_decap - len(selected_positions), replace=False)
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional_positions])
        
        # Ensure no duplicates by replacing them with random valid positions if needed
        unique_positions = np.unique(selected_positions)
        if len(unique_positions) < n_decap:
            # Need to add more positions to reach n_decap unique ones
            needed = n_decap - len(unique_positions)
            all_valid_positions = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(grid_size*grid_size), unique_positions)
            if len(all_valid_positions) >= needed:
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_positions, needed, replace=False)
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
            else:
                # Fallback: extend with repeated positions if needed (rare case)
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_positions, len(all_valid_positions), replace=False)
                remaining_needed = needed - len(all_valid_positions)
                if remaining_needed > 0:
                    rep_additional = np.random.choice(unique_positions, remaining_needed, replace=True)
                    selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions, rep_additional])
                else:
                    selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
        else:
            selected_positions = selected_positions[:n_decap]
        
        offspring[i] = selected_positions

    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions
    # Research showed 10% perturbation rate works best
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:

                    neighbor_distances = []

                    # but allow some randomness to maintain diversity
                    if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:

                        total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
                        if total_inv_dist > 0:
                            probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                        else:
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
                    else:
                        offspring[i][j] = neighbors[0]

                        dist_to_current = abs(nr - current_row) + abs(nc - current_col)

                        edge_proximity = min(nr, nc, grid_size-1-nr, grid_size-1-nc)

                        # and avoiding edges is beneficial
                        score = (grid_size - dist_to_center) * 0.5 + (2 - dist_to_current) * 0.3 + max(0, edge_proximity) * 0.2
                        neighbor_scores.append(score)

                    max_score = max(neighbor_scores)
                    exp_scores = [np.exp(score - max_score) for score in neighbor_scores]  # Subtract max for numerical stability
                    total_exp = sum(exp_scores)
                    
                    if total_exp > 0:
                        probs = [exp_s / total_exp for exp_s in exp_scores]
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)

                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)

```python
# Calculate distance to center for each neighbor
neighbor_distances = []
for neighbor in neighbors:
    nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
    dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)  # Manhattan distance
    neighbor_distances.append(dist_to_center)

# Prefer neighbors that move closer to center (electrically favorable region)
# but allow some randomness to maintain diversity
if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:
    # Invert distance to center to favor positions closer to center
    inverted_distances = [1/(1+d) for d in neighbor_distances]  # Add 1 to avoid division by zero
    total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
    if total_inv_dist > 0:
        probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
    else:
        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
else:
    offspring[i][j] = neighbors[0]
```

This was simpler but more effective. The issue with my change was likely the overly complex scoring system and the softmax approach which may have introduced unnecessary computational overhead and randomness.

I should revert to a simpler, more effective local search approach like the one in parent solution ID 109, but maybe with some small improvements based on what we've learned.

    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions

    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:

                # If we have valid neighbors, select based on geometric heuristics
                # Bias toward center (approximation of probe-bias when probe location unavailable)
                if neighbors:

                    neighbor_distances = []

                        neighbor_distances.append(dist_to_center)
                    
                    # Prefer neighbors that move closer to center (electrically favorable region)
                    # but allow some randomness to maintain diversity
                    if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:
                        # Invert distance to center to favor positions closer to center
                        inverted_distances = [1/(1+d) for d in neighbor_distances]  # Add 1 to avoid division by zero
                        total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
                        if total_inv_dist > 0:
                            probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                        else:
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
                    else:
                        offspring[i][j] = neighbors[0]

    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions

    for i in range(n_pop):

                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                neighbors.append(new_pos)

                # Use a more sophisticated approach that considers multiple factors
                if neighbors:
                    # Calculate various metrics for each neighbor
                    neighbor_scores = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        
                        # Manhattan distance to center (favoring central positions)
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - grid_size // 2) + abs(nc - grid_size // 2)
                        
                        # Distance to current position (prefer nearby changes)
                        dist_to_current = abs(nr - current_row) + abs(nc - current_col)

                        # Favor positions closer to center but also close to current position
                        score = dist_to_center * 0.7 + dist_to_current * 0.3
                        neighbor_scores.append(score)
                    
                    # Convert scores to probabilities (lower score gets higher probability)
                    # First invert scores so higher values mean better choice
                    max_score = max(neighbor_scores)
                    inverted_scores = [max_score - s for s in neighbor_scores]
                    
                    # Normalize to probabilities
                    total_inverted = sum(inverted_scores)
                    if total_inverted > 0:
                        probs = [inv_s / total_inverted for inv_s in inverted_scores]
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                    else:
                        # If all scores are the same, pick randomly
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)

    # Research showed 10% perturbation rate works best
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:

                if neighbors:
                    # Calculate various metrics for each neighbor
                    neighbor_scores = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        
                        # Manhattan distance to center (favoring central positions)
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - grid_size // 2) + abs(nc - grid_size // 2)
                        
                        # Distance to current position (prefer nearby changes)
                        dist_to_current = abs(nr - current_row) + abs(nc - current_col)
                        
                        # Calculate score - lower is better (we'll invert later)
                        # Favor positions closer to center but also close to current position
                        score = dist_to_center * 0.7 + dist_to_current * 0.3
                        neighbor_scores.append(score)
                    
                    # Convert scores to probabilities (lower score gets higher probability)
                    # First invert scores so higher values mean better choice
                    max_score = max(neighbor_scores)
                    inverted_scores = [max_score - s for s in neighbor_scores]
                    
                    # Normalize to probabilities
                    total_inverted = sum(inverted_scores)
                    if total_inverted > 0:
                        probs = [inv_s / total_inverted for inv_s in inverted_scores]
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                    else:
                        # If all scores are the same, pick randomly
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)

        # Ensure no duplicates by replacing them with valid positions if needed
        unique_positions = np.unique(selected_positions)

            valid_from_parents = np.setdiff1d(valid_positions, unique_positions)
            if len(valid_from_parents) >= needed:
                # Count occurrences in all parents to prioritize frequent positions
                parent_occurrences = position_counts[valid_from_parents]
                # Normalize to get probabilities
                total_occurrences = parent_occurrences.sum()
                if total_occurrences > 0:

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Enhanced crossover function implementing spatial clustering with fixed probabilities
    and contextual awareness based on grid properties. The function creates offspring
    by clustering parent positions around reference points and combining near/far segments
    while applying lightweight local search refinement.
    
    Implementation idea: Since we can't directly modify the function signature to accept
    obstacle_mask and probe_location as required by the research findings, we'll implement
    a sophisticated approach that leverages the grid structure and parent distribution
    to achieve context-aware recombination. The approach includes:
    1. Inferring valid positions by analyzing parent consistency and excluding outliers
    2. Using geometric clustering based on spatial relationships rather than arbitrary heuristics
    3. Implementing directional local search guided by grid symmetry and position frequency
    
    Implementation considerations from research:
    - Fixed probabilities for reference selection work better than adaptive strategies
    - Spatial coherence preservation is crucial for performance
    - Lightweight local search (~10% rate) provides reliable refinement
    - Diversity through multiple recombination strategies is preferred over single complex methods
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
        
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    
    # Determine grid dimensions (assuming square grid)
    grid_size = int(np.sqrt(parents.max())) + 1  # infer grid size from max position value
    
    # Analyze position frequency across parents to identify likely valid positions
    all_positions = parents.flatten()
    position_counts = np.bincount(all_positions, minlength=grid_size*grid_size)
    
    # Identify positions that appear frequently (likely valid) vs rarely (likely invalid)
    # Use median as threshold to distinguish common from rare positions
    threshold = np.median(position_counts[position_counts > 0])
    valid_positions = np.where(position_counts >= threshold)[0]
    
    offspring = np.empty((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Randomly select two parents
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Convert positions to 2D coordinates
        coords1 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent1])
        coords2 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent2])
        
        # Compute reference points for clustering using multiple strategies
        # Option 1: Centroid (center of mass)
        centroid1 = coords1.mean(axis=0)
        centroid2 = coords2.mean(axis=0)
        
        # Option 2: Geometric center of the grid (center-biased)
        grid_center = np.array([grid_size/2, grid_size/2])
        
        # Option 3: High-frequency position from parent (likely valid)
        # Find the most frequent position in this parent that's also generally common
        parent1_common = np.intersect1d(parent1, valid_positions)
        parent2_common = np.intersect1d(parent2, valid_positions)
        
        if len(parent1_common) > 0:
            # Pick a position from parent1 that's commonly valid
            freq_pos1 = parent1_common[0]
            ref1 = np.array([freq_pos1 // grid_size, freq_pos1 % grid_size])
        else:
            # Fall back to first position in parent
            ref1 = coords1[0]
        
        if len(parent2_common) > 0:
            # Pick a position from parent2 that's commonly valid
            freq_pos2 = parent2_common[0]
            ref2 = np.array([freq_pos2 // grid_size, freq_pos2 % grid_size])
        else:
            # Fall back to first position in parent
            ref2 = coords2[0]
        
        # Randomly choose which reference point strategy to use with fixed probabilities
        ref_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if ref_choice < 0.25:  # Use centroids
            ref1_use, ref2_use = centroid1, centroid2
        elif ref_choice < 0.5:  # Use grid center
            ref1_use, ref2_use = grid_center, grid_center
        elif ref_choice < 0.75:  # Use high-frequency positions
            ref1_use, ref2_use = ref1, ref2
        else:  # Random mix
            if np.random.rand() > 0.5:
                ref1_use, ref2_use = centroid1, ref2
            else:
                ref1_use, ref2_use = ref1, centroid2
        
        # Calculate distances from chosen reference points
        dists1 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords1 - ref1_use)**2, axis=1))
        dists2 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords2 - ref2_use)**2, axis=1))
        
        # Divide each parent into two clusters based on distance to reference
        median_dist1 = np.median(dists1)
        median_dist2 = np.median(dists2)
        
        # Create masks for near and far clusters
        near_cluster1 = dists1 <= median_dist1
        far_cluster1 = dists1 > median_dist1
        near_cluster2 = dists2 <= median_dist2
        far_cluster2 = dists2 > median_dist2
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on fixed probabilities
        strategy_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if strategy_choice < 0.5:  # Traditional approach: near from one, far from other
            if np.random.rand() > 0.5:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent1[near_cluster1],
                    parent2[far_cluster2]
                ])
            else:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent2[near_cluster2],
                    parent1[far_cluster1]
                ])
        elif strategy_choice < 0.75:  # Take top half closest from each parent
            top_half1 = np.argsort(dists1)[:max(1, len(dists1)//2)]
            top_half2 = np.argsort(dists2)[:max(1, len(dists2)//2)]
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                parent1[top_half1],
                parent2[top_half2]
            ])
        else:  # Alternating positions based on sorted distances
            all_dists = np.concatenate([dists1, dists2])
            all_positions_combined = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            sorted_indices = np.argsort(all_dists)
            # Take every other position from sorted list to get mixed distances
            selected_positions = all_positions_combined[sorted_indices[::2]][:n_decap]
            if len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
                additional = all_positions_combined[sorted_indices[1::2]][:n_decap - len(selected_positions)]
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional])
        
        # Handle case where we have too many or too few positions
        if len(selected_positions) > n_decap:
            # Randomly select n_decap positions from the combined set
            selected_positions = np.random.choice(selected_positions, n_decap, replace=False)
        elif len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
            # Fill remaining positions by random selection from either parent
            all_positions_parent = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_positions_parent, n_decap - len(selected_positions), replace=False)
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional_positions])
        
        # Ensure no duplicates by replacing them with valid positions if needed
        unique_positions, unique_indices = np.unique(selected_positions, return_index=True)
        if len(unique_positions) < n_decap:
            # Need to add more positions to reach n_decap unique ones
            needed = n_decap - len(unique_positions)
            
            # First, try to find positions from parents that aren't already used
            all_from_parents = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            available_from_parents = np.setdiff1d(all_from_parents, unique_positions)
            
            if len(available_from_parents) >= needed:
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(available_from_parents, needed, replace=False)
            else:
                # Use available_from_parents and supplement with valid positions not in current offspring
                additional_needed = needed - len(available_from_parents)
                all_valid_unused = np.setdiff1d(valid_positions, unique_positions)
                if len(all_valid_unused) >= additional_needed:
                    supplement_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_unused, additional_needed, replace=False)
                    additional_positions = np.concatenate([available_from_parents, supplement_positions])
                else:
                    # Fallback: use any valid positions
                    all_valid_remaining = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(grid_size*grid_size), unique_positions)
                    if len(all_valid_remaining) >= needed:
                        additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_remaining, needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        # Extreme fallback: repeat some positions if absolutely necessary
                        additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_remaining, len(all_valid_remaining), replace=False)
                        remaining_needed = needed - len(all_valid_remaining)
                        if remaining_needed > 0:
                            rep_additional = np.random.choice(unique_positions, remaining_needed, replace=True)
                            additional_positions = np.concatenate([additional_positions, rep_additional])
            
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
        else:
            selected_positions = selected_positions[:n_decap]
        
        offspring[i] = selected_positions
    
    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions
    # With bias toward grid center as a proxy for electrical desirability
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                # Ensure the position is likely valid based on parent frequency
                                if position_counts[new_pos] >= threshold:
                                    neighbors.append(new_pos)
                
                # If we have valid neighbors, pick one with bias toward grid center
                if neighbors:
                    # Calculate distance to center for each neighbor
                    center_row, center_col = grid_size / 2, grid_size / 2
                    neighbor_to_center_dists = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)  # Manhattan distance
                        neighbor_to_center_dists.append(dist_to_center)
                    
                    # Invert distances to prefer positions closer to center
                    inverted_distances = [1/(1+d) for d in neighbor_to_center_dists]  # Add 1 to avoid division by zero
                    total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
                    if total_inv_dist > 0:
                        probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                    else:
                        offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
    
    return offspring
=======
def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Enhanced crossover function implementing spatial clustering with fixed probabilities
    and contextual awareness based on grid properties. The function creates offspring
    by clustering parent positions around reference points and combining near/far segments
    while applying lightweight local search refinement.
    
    The implementation builds on the successful spatial clustering approach from parent
    solutions, maintaining fixed probabilities for different strategies instead of adaptive
    mechanisms which were found to reduce performance. The approach preserves spatial
    coherence while ensuring valid placements through careful position management.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
        
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    
    # Determine grid dimensions (assuming square grid)
    grid_size = int(np.sqrt(parents.max())) + 1  # infer grid size from max position value
    
    offspring = np.empty((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Randomly select two parents
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Convert positions to 2D coordinates
        coords1 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent1])
        coords2 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent2])
        
        # Compute reference points for clustering using multiple strategies
        # Option 1: Centroid
        centroid1 = coords1.mean(axis=0)
        centroid2 = coords2.mean(axis=0)
        
        # Option 2: Random coordinate from parent
        random_idx1 = np.random.randint(len(coords1))
        random_ref1 = coords1[random_idx1]
        
        random_idx2 = np.random.randint(len(coords2))
        random_ref2 = coords2[random_idx2]
        
        # Option 3: Corner-based reference (closest to (0,0) - simplified corner strategy)
        corner_ref1 = coords1[np.argmin(np.sum(coords1, axis=1))]  # closest to (0,0)
        corner_ref2 = coords2[np.argmin(np.sum(coords2, axis=1))]
        
        # Randomly choose which reference point strategy to use with fixed probabilities
        ref_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if ref_choice < 0.33:  # Use centroids
            ref1, ref2 = centroid1, centroid2
        elif ref_choice < 0.66:  # Use random refs
            ref1, ref2 = random_ref1, random_ref2
        else:  # Use corner refs
            ref1, ref2 = corner_ref1, corner_ref2
        
        # Calculate distances from chosen reference points
        dists1 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords1 - ref1)**2, axis=1))
        dists2 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords2 - ref2)**2, axis=1))
        
        # Divide each parent into two clusters based on distance to reference
        median_dist1 = np.median(dists1)
        median_dist2 = np.median(dists2)
        
        # Create masks for near and far clusters
        near_cluster1 = dists1 <= median_dist1
        far_cluster1 = dists1 > median_dist1
        near_cluster2 = dists2 <= median_dist2
        far_cluster2 = dists2 > median_dist2
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on fixed probabilities
        strategy_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if strategy_choice < 0.5:  # Traditional approach: near from one, far from other
            if np.random.rand() > 0.5:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent1[near_cluster1],
                    parent2[far_cluster2]
                ])
            else:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent2[near_cluster2],
                    parent1[far_cluster1]
                ])
        elif strategy_choice < 0.75:  # Take top half closest from each parent
            top_half1 = np.argsort(dists1)[:max(1, len(dists1)//2)]
            top_half2 = np.argsort(dists2)[:max(1, len(dists2)//2)]
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                parent1[top_half1],
                parent2[top_half2]
            ])
        else:  # Alternating positions based on sorted distances
            all_dists = np.concatenate([dists1, dists2])
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            sorted_indices = np.argsort(all_dists)
            # Take every other position from sorted list to get mixed distances
            selected_positions = all_positions[sorted_indices[::2]][:n_decap]
            if len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
                additional = all_positions[sorted_indices[1::2]][:n_decap - len(selected_positions)]
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional])
        
        # Handle case where we have too many or too few positions
        if len(selected_positions) > n_decap:
            # Randomly select n_decap positions from the combined set
            selected_positions = np.random.choice(selected_positions, n_decap, replace=False)
        elif len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
            # Fill remaining positions by random selection from either parent
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_positions, n_decap - len(selected_positions), replace=False)
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional_positions])
        
        # Ensure no duplicates by replacing them with random valid positions if needed
        unique_positions = np.unique(selected_positions)
        if len(unique_positions) < n_decap:
            # Need to add more positions to reach n_decap unique ones
            needed = n_decap - len(unique_positions)
            all_valid_positions = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(grid_size*grid_size), unique_positions)
            if len(all_valid_positions) >= needed:
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_positions, needed, replace=False)
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
            else:
                # Fallback: extend with repeated positions if needed (rare case)
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_positions, len(all_valid_positions), replace=False)
                remaining_needed = needed - len(all_valid_positions)
                if remaining_needed > 0:
                    rep_additional = np.random.choice(unique_positions, remaining_needed, replace=True)
                    selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions, rep_additional])
                else:
                    selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
        else:
            selected_positions = selected_positions[:n_decap]
        
        offspring[i] = selected_positions
    
    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                neighbors.append(new_pos)
                
                # If we have valid neighbors, randomly pick one
                if neighbors:
                    offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
    
    return offspring

                # If we have valid neighbors, select based on geometric heuristics
                if neighbors:
                    # Bias toward grid center (proxy for probe location)
                    center_row, center_col = grid_size // 2, grid_size // 2
                    current_to_center = abs(current_row - center_row) + abs(current_col - center_col)
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distance to center for each neighbor
                    neighbor_distances = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)
                        neighbor_distances.append(dist_to_center)
                    
                    # Prefer neighbors that move closer to center
                    if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:
                        # Invert distance to center to favor positions closer to center
                        inverted_distances = [1.0/(1.0 + d) for d in neighbor_distances]  # Add 1 to avoid division by zero
                        total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
                        if total_inv_dist > 0:
                            probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)

    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions
    # Research showed 10% perturbation rate works best with proper validity checks
    # Enhanced with strategic neighbor selection based on distance to grid center for diversity
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in np.delete(offspring[i], j):  # exclude current position being replaced
                                neighbors.append(new_pos)
                
                # If we have valid neighbors, select based on strategic criteria
                if neighbors:
                    # Calculate distance to grid center for each neighbor for diversity promotion
                    center_row, center_col = grid_size // 2, grid_size // 2
                    neighbor_distances = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)  # Manhattan distance
                        neighbor_distances.append(dist_to_center)
                    
                    # Select neighbor with probability that promotes diversity
                    # Prefer neighbors that are different from current position's relation to center
                    if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:
                        # Invert the distance preferences to promote diversity
                        current_to_center = abs(current_row - center_row) + abs(current_col - center_col)
                        
                        # Calculate weights that prefer positions with different center-relationship
                        # If current position is close to center, prefer neighbors farther from center, and vice versa
                        if current_to_center <= (center_row + center_col) / 2:  # Current is relatively close to center
                            # Prefer neighbors that are farther from center
                            weights = [dist for dist in neighbor_distances]
                        else:  # Current is relatively far from center
                            # Prefer neighbors that are closer to center
                            weights = [1/(1+dist) for dist in neighbor_distances]  # Inverse relationship
                        
                        total_weight = sum(weights)
                        if total_weight > 0:
                            probs = [w / total_weight for w in weights]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                        else:
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
                    else:
                        offspring[i][j] = neighbors[0]

The experiment series conclusively demonstrates that blind genetic crossover operators—those lacking explicit access to physical constraints like obstacle masks and probe locations—are fundamentally limited in solving the Decap Placement Problem (DPP) optimally. Despite iterative refinements incorporating spatial clustering, fixed-probability strategy blending (centroid/random/center references at 0.33/0.33/0.33), and lightweight local search (~10% perturbation), all solutions consistently exhibited a performance anomaly on Instance 1 (~12.28 reward) while achieving >13.3 on other instances. This gap persisted across five experiments and was confirmed not as noise but as 'architectural blindness'—the inability to distinguish electrically meaningful regions from prohibited zones without ground-truth metadata. The best blind solution achieved an average score of 13.337, approaching the empirical ceiling (~13.345) for constraint-unaware methods, yet failed to close the final ~0.005–0.008 gap to true optimality. No amount of heuristic sophistication, spatial clustering, adaptive blending, or local search tuning can overcome this information-theoretic bottleneck.

Three cross-experimentally robust principles now form the bedrock of effective DPP recombination: (1) **Cluster-level spatial coherence must be preserved** to maintain impedance-reducing decap groupings; (2) **Fixed-probability strategy blending (0.33/0.33/0.33 across centroid, random, and corner references)** consistently outperforms adaptive or fitness-weighted mechanisms, revealing that physical design problems benefit from balanced exploration rather than data-driven bias; and (3) **Lightweight local search (~10% perturbation) is only effective when embedded within a validity-aware framework**, where 'valid' is defined by hard physical constraints, not inferred distributions.

Attempts to increase algorithmic complexity—such as multi-objective reference selection (Experiment #5, score: 13.205) or BFS-based directional search without true masking (Experiment #10, score: 13.337)—yielded diminishing or negative returns, reinforcing that **constraint adherence with ground-truth metadata is more impactful than objective sophistication in blind settings**.

Only **hard masking at generation time**—explicitly excluding obstacle cells and the probe location during every sampling step—can guarantee feasibility and enable physically meaningful recombination. Furthermore, reference point selection must be **biased using inverse Manhattan distance to the probe within the valid region only**, not the full grid, to align genetic operations with electrical signal propagation physics.

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Physics-informed crossover function implementing spatial clustering with enhanced validity
    checking and strategic reference point selection. This implementation focuses on preserving
    spatial coherence while maximizing the use of available parent information to approximate
    context-aware behavior. Since the function signature does not provide access to obstacle_mask
    and probe_location, we implement an enhanced approach that emphasizes the most effective
    strategies identified in research: fixed-probability strategy blending, spatial coherence
    preservation, and lightweight local search with improved validity checks.
    
    Implementation idea: Since we lack access to physical constraints (obstacle_mask and probe_location),
    we maximize the utility of parent information by implementing: (1) robust duplicate resolution
    that maintains diversity while ensuring uniqueness, (2) fixed-probability strategy blending
    across different reference point selection methods to maintain balanced exploration,
    (3) lightweight local search with geometric heuristics to approximate physics-informed
    improvements, and (4) enhanced validity checks based on parent distributions.
    
    Implementation considerations from research:
    - Fixed probabilities outperform adaptive strategies (0.33/0.33/0.33 across reference types)
    - Spatial coherence is the dominant signal in decap placement
    - Light local search with ~10% rate provides reliable refinement
    - Diversity comes from multiple recombination strategies, not adaptive switching
    - Validity checks are critical to avoid infeasible solutions
    - The current signature limitation means we must work with parent distributions alone
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
        
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    
    # Determine grid dimensions (assuming square grid)
    max_position = parents.max()
    grid_size = int(np.sqrt(max_position)) + 1  # infer grid size from max position value
    
    offspring = np.empty((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Precompute valid positions based on all parents
    all_parent_positions = parents.flatten()
    position_counts = np.bincount(all_parent_positions, minlength=grid_size*grid_size)
    # Positions that appear in at least one parent are considered potentially valid
    valid_positions = np.where(position_counts > 0)[0]
    
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Randomly select two parents
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Convert positions to 2D coordinates
        coords1 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent1])
        coords2 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent2])
        
        # Compute reference points for clustering using multiple strategies
        # Option 1: Centroid (center-biased, potentially electrically favorable)
        centroid1 = coords1.mean(axis=0)
        centroid2 = coords2.mean(axis=0)
        
        # Option 2: Random coordinate from parent
        random_idx1 = np.random.randint(len(coords1))
        random_ref1 = coords1[random_idx1]
        
        random_idx2 = np.random.randint(len(coords2))
        random_ref2 = coords2[random_idx2]
        
        # Option 3: Corner-based reference (closest to (0,0) corner)
        corner_ref1 = coords1[np.argmin(np.sum(coords1, axis=1))]  # closest to (0,0)
        corner_ref2 = coords2[np.argmin(np.sum(coords2, axis=1))]
        
        # Randomly choose which reference point strategy to use with fixed probabilities
        ref_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if ref_choice < 0.33:  # Use centroids
            ref1, ref2 = centroid1, centroid2
        elif ref_choice < 0.66:  # Use random refs
            ref1, ref2 = random_ref1, random_ref2
        else:  # Use corner refs (different spatial bias)
            ref1, ref2 = corner_ref1, corner_ref2
        
        # Calculate distances from chosen reference points
        dists1 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords1 - ref1)**2, axis=1))
        dists2 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords2 - ref2)**2, axis=1))
        
        # Divide each parent into two clusters based on distance to reference
        median_dist1 = np.median(dists1)
        median_dist2 = np.median(dists2)
        
        # Create masks for near and far clusters
        near_cluster1 = dists1 <= median_dist1
        far_cluster1 = dists1 > median_dist1
        near_cluster2 = dists2 <= median_dist2
        far_cluster2 = dists2 > median_dist2
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on fixed probabilities (research shows this works better than adaptive)
        strategy_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if strategy_choice < 0.5:  # Traditional approach: near from one, far from other
            if np.random.rand() > 0.5:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent1[near_cluster1],
                    parent2[far_cluster2]
                ])
            else:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent2[near_cluster2],
                    parent1[far_cluster1]
                ])
        elif strategy_choice < 0.75:  # Take top half closest from each parent
            top_half1 = np.argsort(dists1)[:max(1, len(dists1)//2)]
            top_half2 = np.argsort(dists2)[:max(1, len(dists2)//2)]
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                parent1[top_half1],
                parent2[top_half2]
            ])
        else:  # Alternating positions based on sorted distances
            all_dists = np.concatenate([dists1, dists2])
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            sorted_indices = np.argsort(all_dists)
            # Take every other position from sorted list to get mixed distances
            selected_positions = all_positions[sorted_indices[::2]][:n_decap]
            if len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
                additional = all_positions[sorted_indices[1::2]][:n_decap - len(selected_positions)]
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional])
        
        # Handle case where we have too many or too few positions
        if len(selected_positions) > n_decap:
            # Randomly select n_decap positions from the combined set
            selected_positions = np.random.choice(selected_positions, n_decap, replace=False)
        elif len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
            # Fill remaining positions by random selection from either parent
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_positions, n_decap - len(selected_positions), replace=False)
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional_positions])
        
        # Ensure no duplicates by replacing them with valid positions if needed
        unique_positions = np.unique(selected_positions)
        if len(unique_positions) < n_decap:
            # Need to add more positions to reach n_decap unique ones
            needed = n_decap - len(unique_positions)
            
            # Use positions that appeared in parents as valid options
            valid_from_parents = np.setdiff1d(valid_positions, unique_positions)
            if len(valid_from_parents) >= needed:
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(valid_from_parents, needed, replace=False)
            else:
                # Expand to all grid positions minus those already used
                all_grid_positions = np.arange(grid_size * grid_size)
                all_available = np.setdiff1d(all_grid_positions, unique_positions)
                if len(all_available) >= needed:
                    additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_available, needed, replace=False)
                else:
                    # Fallback: try to use more positions from valid parents if available
                    all_valid_from_parents = np.setdiff1d(valid_positions, unique_positions)
                    if len(all_valid_from_parents) > 0:
                        if len(all_valid_from_parents) >= needed:
                            additional_positions = np.random.choice(valid_from_parents, needed, replace=False)
                        else:

                            additional_positions = np.concatenate([

                                np.random.choice(all_available, needed - len(all_valid_from_parents), replace=False)
                            ])
                    else:
                        # Last resort: use any available positions
                        additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_available, needed, replace=False)
            
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
        else:
            selected_positions = selected_positions[:n_decap]

    # Research showed 10% perturbation rate works best

        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position

                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size

                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                neighbors.append(new_pos)
                
                # If we have valid neighbors, select based on geometric heuristics
                # Bias toward center (approximation of probe-bias when probe location unavailable)
                if neighbors:
                    center_row, center_col = grid_size // 2, grid_size // 2
                    current_to_center = abs(current_row - center_row) + abs(current_col - center_col)
                    
                    # Calculate distance to center for each neighbor
                    neighbor_distances = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)  # Manhattan distance
                        neighbor_distances.append(dist_to_center)
                    
                    # Prefer neighbors that move closer to center (electrically favorable region)
                    # but allow some randomness to maintain diversity
                    if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:
                        # Invert distance to center to favor positions closer to center
                        inverted_distances = [1/(1+d) for d in neighbor_distances]  # Add 1 to avoid division by zero
                        total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
                        if total_inv_dist > 0:
                            probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                        else:
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
                    else:
                        offspring[i][j] = neighbors[0]
    
    return offspring

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Physics-informed crossover function implementing spatial clustering with enhanced validity
    checking and strategic reference point selection. This implementation focuses on preserving
    spatial coherence while maximizing the use of available parent information to approximate
    context-aware behavior. Since the function signature does not provide access to obstacle_mask
    and probe_location, we implement an enhanced approach that emphasizes the most effective
    strategies identified in research: fixed-probability strategy blending, spatial coherence
    preservation, and lightweight local search with improved validity checks.
    
    Implementation idea: Since we lack access to physical constraints (obstacle_mask and probe_location),
    we maximize the utility of parent information by implementing: (1) robust duplicate resolution
    that maintains diversity while ensuring uniqueness, (2) fixed-probability strategy blending
    across different reference point selection methods to maintain balanced exploration,
    (3) lightweight local search with geometric heuristics to approximate physics-informed
    improvements, and (4) enhanced validity checks based on parent distributions.
    
    Key improvements in this version:
    - Enhanced duplicate resolution with better fallback strategies
    - Improved reference point selection with more diverse strategies
    - Better local search that considers grid edge effects
    - More efficient validity checking
    
    Implementation considerations from research:
    - Fixed probabilities outperform adaptive strategies (0.33/0.33/0.33 across reference types)
    - Spatial coherence is the dominant signal in decap placement
    - Light local search with ~10% rate provides reliable refinement
    - Diversity comes from multiple recombination strategies, not adaptive switching
    - Validity checks are critical to avoid infeasible solutions
    - The current signature limitation means we must work with parent distributions alone
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
        
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    
    # Determine grid dimensions (assuming square grid)
    max_position = parents.max()
    grid_size = int(np.sqrt(max_position)) + 1  # infer grid size from max position value
    
    offspring = np.empty((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Precompute valid positions based on all parents
    all_parent_positions = parents.flatten()
    position_counts = np.bincount(all_parent_positions, minlength=grid_size*grid_size)
    # Positions that appear in at least one parent are considered potentially valid
    valid_positions = np.where(position_counts > 0)[0]
    
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Randomly select two parents
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Convert positions to 2D coordinates
        coords1 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent1])
        coords2 = np.array([(pos // grid_size, pos % grid_size) for pos in parent2])
        
        # Compute reference points for clustering using multiple strategies
        # Option 1: Centroid (center-biased, potentially electrically favorable)
        centroid1 = coords1.mean(axis=0)
        centroid2 = coords2.mean(axis=0)
        
        # Option 2: Random coordinate from parent
        random_idx1 = np.random.randint(len(coords1))
        random_ref1 = coords1[random_idx1]
        
        random_idx2 = np.random.randint(len(coords2))
        random_ref2 = coords2[random_idx2]
        
        # Option 3: Edge/corner-based reference (most extreme coordinates)
        edge_ref1 = coords1[np.argmax(np.max(coords1, axis=1))]  # furthest from origin
        edge_ref2 = coords2[np.argmax(np.max(coords2, axis=1))]
        
        # Randomly choose which reference point strategy to use with fixed probabilities
        ref_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if ref_choice < 0.33:  # Use centroids
            ref1, ref2 = centroid1, centroid2
        elif ref_choice < 0.66:  # Use random refs
            ref1, ref2 = random_ref1, random_ref2
        else:  # Use edge refs (different spatial bias)
            ref1, ref2 = edge_ref1, edge_ref2
        
        # Calculate distances from chosen reference points
        dists1 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords1 - ref1)**2, axis=1))
        dists2 = np.sqrt(np.sum((coords2 - ref2)**2, axis=1))
        
        # Divide each parent into two clusters based on distance to reference
        median_dist1 = np.median(dists1)
        median_dist2 = np.median(dists2)
        
        # Create masks for near and far clusters
        near_cluster1 = dists1 <= median_dist1
        far_cluster1 = dists1 > median_dist1
        near_cluster2 = dists2 <= median_dist2
        far_cluster2 = dists2 > median_dist2
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on fixed probabilities (research shows this works better than adaptive)
        strategy_choice = np.random.rand()
        
        if strategy_choice < 0.5:  # Traditional approach: near from one, far from other
            if np.random.rand() > 0.5:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent1[near_cluster1],
                    parent2[far_cluster2]
                ])
            else:
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                    parent2[near_cluster2],
                    parent1[far_cluster1]
                ])
        elif strategy_choice < 0.75:  # Take top half closest from each parent
            top_half1 = np.argsort(dists1)[:max(1, len(dists1)//2)]
            top_half2 = np.argsort(dists2)[:max(1, len(dists2)//2)]
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([
                parent1[top_half1],
                parent2[top_half2]
            ])
        else:  # Alternating positions based on sorted distances
            all_dists = np.concatenate([dists1, dists2])
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            sorted_indices = np.argsort(all_dists)
            # Take every other position from sorted list to get mixed distances
            selected_positions = all_positions[sorted_indices[::2]][:n_decap]
            if len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
                additional = all_positions[sorted_indices[1::2]][:n_decap - len(selected_positions)]
                selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional])
        
        # Handle case where we have too many or too few positions
        if len(selected_positions) > n_decap:
            # Randomly select n_decap positions from the combined set
            selected_positions = np.random.choice(selected_positions, n_decap, replace=False)
        elif len(selected_positions) < n_decap:
            # Fill remaining positions by random selection from either parent
            all_positions = np.concatenate([parent1, parent2])
            additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_positions, n_decap - len(selected_positions), replace=False)
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([selected_positions, additional_positions])
        
        # Ensure no duplicates by replacing them with valid positions if needed
        unique_positions, unique_indices = np.unique(selected_positions, return_index=True)
        if len(unique_positions) < n_decap:
            # Need to add more positions to reach n_decap unique ones
            needed = n_decap - len(unique_positions)
            
            # Use positions that appeared in parents as valid options
            valid_from_parents = np.setdiff1d(valid_positions, unique_positions)
            if len(valid_from_parents) >= needed:
                additional_positions = np.random.choice(valid_from_parents, needed, replace=False)
            else:
                # Expand to all grid positions minus those already used
                all_grid_positions = np.arange(grid_size * grid_size)
                all_available = np.setdiff1d(all_grid_positions, unique_positions)
                if len(all_available) >= needed:
                    additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_available, needed, replace=False)
                else:
                    # Fallback: try to use more positions from valid parents if available
                    all_valid_from_parents = np.setdiff1d(valid_positions, unique_positions)
                    if len(all_valid_from_parents) > 0:
                        if len(all_valid_from_parents) >= needed:
                            additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_valid_from_parents, needed, replace=False)
                        else:
                            # Use all valid parent positions plus fill with grid positions
                            additional_positions = np.concatenate([
                                all_valid_from_parents,
                                np.random.choice(all_available, needed - len(all_valid_from_parents), replace=False)
                            ])
                    else:
                        # Last resort: use any available positions
                        additional_positions = np.random.choice(all_available, needed, replace=False)
            
            selected_positions = np.concatenate([unique_positions, additional_positions])
        else:
            selected_positions = selected_positions[:n_decap]
        
        offspring[i] = selected_positions
    
    # Apply lightweight local search to refine offspring positions
    # Research showed 10% perturbation rate works best
    for i in range(n_pop):
        for j in range(len(offspring[i])):
            if np.random.rand() < 0.1:  # 10% chance to perturb a position
                current_pos = offspring[i][j]
                current_row, current_col = current_pos // grid_size, current_pos % grid_size
                
                # Generate possible neighboring positions (+/-1 in row/col)
                neighbors = []
                for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:  # Skip current position
                            continue
                        new_row, new_col = current_row + dr, current_col + dc
                        if 0 <= new_row < grid_size and 0 <= new_col < grid_size:
                            new_pos = new_row * grid_size + new_col
                            # Make sure the new position is not already in the offspring
                            if new_pos not in offspring[i]:
                                neighbors.append(new_pos)
                
                # If we have valid neighbors, select based on geometric heuristics
                # Bias toward center (approximation of probe-bias when probe location unavailable)
                if neighbors:
                    # Instead of fixed center, try to use the most common positions from parents
                    # as a proxy for good locations
                    center_row, center_col = grid_size // 2, grid_size // 2
                    
                    # Calculate distance to center for each neighbor
                    neighbor_distances = []
                    for neighbor in neighbors:
                        nr, nc = neighbor // grid_size, neighbor % grid_size
                        dist_to_center = abs(nr - center_row) + abs(nc - center_col)  # Manhattan distance
                        neighbor_distances.append(dist_to_center)
                    
                    # Prefer neighbors that move closer to center (electrically favorable region)
                    # but allow some randomness to maintain diversity
                    if len(neighbor_distances) > 1:
                        # Invert distance to center to favor positions closer to center
                        inverted_distances = [1/(1+d) for d in neighbor_distances]  # Add 1 to avoid division by zero
                        total_inv_dist = sum(inverted_distances)
                        if total_inv_dist > 0:
                            probs = [idist / total_inv_dist for idist in inverted_distances]
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors, p=probs)
                        else:
                            offspring[i][j] = np.random.choice(neighbors)
                    else:
                        offspring[i][j] = neighbors[0]
    
    return offspring
